The minor of $b_{21} = 3$ (second row, first column) is the determinant of the remaining entries when the column and row containing $3$ are removed: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075201/assets/a69955fcba387ef3c65f1c1529c2007d8d70f82d95738af9b995999a21198730.png)

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 7 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot 2-5\cdot 7 \\  & =2-35 \\  & =-33.\end{aligned}
$$

e-4441.problem:
Given that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ find all the possible values of $k$ in the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075201/assets/1d37ba9039f24a96be2d148c9f30c8a10ca30c9745ad8a28df23de5a42f6dcab.png)
e-4441.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and third column:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14075201/assets/80f9b95139f7b571c7752ee1feec4c9d3df8456223581736ae019344a6f9a080.png)

The minor of $a_{23}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot 2k-3\cdot (-1) \\  & =2{k}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{k}^{2}+3 & =5 \\ 2{k}^{2} & =2 \\ {k}^{2} & =1 \\ k & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $k=-1$ and $k=1.$

after.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and second column:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2k & ∗ & 6 \\ ∗ & 5 & ∗ \\ 11 & ∗ & k+3\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${a}_{22}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}2k & 6 \\ 11 & k+3\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}2k & 6 \\ 11 & k+3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2k\cdot (k+3)-11\cdot 6 \\  & =2{k}^{2}+6k-66.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${a}_{22}$ is $-70$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{k}^{2}+6k-66 & =-70 \\ 2{k}^{2}+6k+4 & =0 \\ {k}^{2}+3k+2 & =0 \\ (k+1)(k+2) & =0\end{aligned}

content.problem:
Given that the minor of ${a}_{22}$ is $-70$, find all the possible values of $k$ in the matrix

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2k & -8 & 6 \\ 0 & 5 & -7 \\ 11 & 9 & k+3\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and second column:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2k & ∗ & 6 \\ ∗ & 5 & ∗ \\ 11 & ∗ & k+3\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${a}_{22}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}2k & 6 \\ 11 & k+3\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}2k & 6 \\ 11 & k+3\end{aligned}| \\  & =2k\cdot (k+3)-11\cdot 6 \\  & =2{k}^{2}+6k-66.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${a}_{22}$ is $-70$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{k}^{2}+6k-66 & =-70 \\ 2{k}^{2}+6k+4 & =0 \\ {k}^{2}+3k+2 & =0 \\ (k+1)(k+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $k=-1$ and $k=-2.$

B=[\begin{aligned}6 & -{x}^{2} & -10 \\ -5 & 8 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}].

content.worked_solution:
First, we remove the third row and third column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}6 & -{x}^{2} & ∗ \\ -5 & 8 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${b}_{33}$ is

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}6 & -{x}^{2} \\ -5 & 8\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}6 & -{x}^{2} \\ -5 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =6\cdot 8-(-5)\cdot (-{x}^{2}) \\  & =48-5{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${b}_{33}$ is $3$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}48-5{x}^{2} & =3 \\ 45-5{x}^{2} & =0 \\ 9-{x}^{2} & =0 \\ (3-x)(3+x) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=-3$ and $x=3.$
